{{short description|Swiss mathematician}}
'''Louis Jacques Crelier''' (3 November 1873, [[Bure, Switzerland]] – 28 November 1935) was a Swiss mathematician.<ref name=DIJU>{{cite web|title=Crelier, Louis-Jacques (1873–1935)|website=Dictionnaire du Jura.ch (diju.ch)|url=http://diju.ch/notices/detail/4295}}</ref>

In 1886 he enrolled at l'Ecole normale in [[Porrentruy]] and then studied at the [[University of Berne]], where he received his doctorate in 1895. He began his teaching career at the secondary school in [[Saint-Imier]] and then taught at the technical school (founded in 1873) in [[Biel/Bienne]]. He became in 1912 professor extraordinarius and in 1918 professor ordinarius at the University of Berne.<ref name=DIJU/>

Crelier served a two-year term from 1920 to 1921 as president of the [[Swiss Mathematical Society]]. He was an Invited Speaker of the [[International Congress of Mathematicians|ICM]] in 1924 at Toronto<ref>{{cite book|author=Crelier, L. J.|chapter=Observations pratiques de méthodologie|title=''In:'' Proceedings of the International Congress of Mathematicians in Toronto, August 11–16. 1924|volume=2|pages=973–974|chapter-url=http://www.mathunion.org/ICM/ICM1924.2/Main/icm1924.2.0973.0974.ocr.pdf}}</ref> and in 1928 at Bologna.<ref>{{cite book|author=Crelier, L.|chapter=Sur quelques familles de courbes considérées au point de vue cinématique: astroïdes ed cornoïdes|title=''In:'' Atti del Congresso Internazionale dei Matematici: Bologna del 3 al 10 de settembre di 1928|volume=4|pages=413–418|chapter-url=http://www.mathunion.org/ICM/ICM1928.4/Main/icm1928.4.0413.0418.ocr.pdf}}</ref>
